entries.place: Lisette's service room and the master suite, Redmist Estate
entries.what_happened: Lisette opened the plain-latched door, duster held like a shield, and said the rooms were aired but the west drapes wanted mending. Julian said he would not inspect drapes from the hall and asked what she thought needed doing. She led him into the master suite and named three things: the east bath water runs cold until the boiler warms, the garden-side window latch is loose and should not be leaned on, and the mattress is new. Asked what a decade of watching had shown, she said the west corridor ceiling has a wet patch patched twice since autumn with nothing above it examined, and that a key on the house ring fits no door she has found in ten years. The house ring hangs in the pantry by the back stairs. The wet patch is above the linen store, whose ceiling hatch is painted shut; the attic stair on that side was boarded over before her time, with rusted nails. She said she was sixteen when Mrs. Doyle boxed her ear for asking and told her Westons ask, Franklins serve, and that she feared what would be said of the maid who went up. Julian promised the telling would be hers to choose and asked her to refuse any task that cost her too much. She said the key should be in his pocket before the light fails, after the kitchen turns down and before the night staff come up, or tomorrow morning if Jezebel kept him. She warned the attic stair was boarded rather than mended for a reason: the year it was boarded, Bernard had tradesmen in the west study for a month, paid from his own pocket, not the estate accounts, and the old cook said he would not let the housekeeper carry a tea tray up. She heard him argue with Mrs. Doyle through the door, catching only that the house had already paid enough for his mistakes; Mrs. Doyle came out white and never spoke of it. She had never repeated it to anyone. Julian said he would not mention it to Jezebel and would come find her after the kitchen turned down, or tomorrow morning. She told him the third step creaks.

entries.place: Redmist Estate main hall, at the wide desk
entries.what_happened: Julian came down to the main hall, where tea things had appeared, the lilies had been moved into the morning sun, and Gabriella's voice was heard seeing off a departing visitor before the front door closed. Jezebel waited at the wide desk with the leather folder open, a pen beside it and a cold cup of coffee, and told him to sit or stand with the window at his back so she could see his face. Julian took the chair and asked how much of the money was not his, what happened to the rest, and whether there was a way out of the debts that did not gut the foundations. Jezebel said the debt was about seven hundred and forty thousand: Bernard borrowed against the east pasture twenty years back and again ten years later, the second loan drawn in a lump with no schedule or project attached, interest paid regularly until eight weeks before he died, leaving the estate two payments behind and the lender's man sending sharp letters. The foundations are ring-fenced in the will, but the estate's liquidity is not, so the choice is to sell something or borrow again, and she wanted his reasons in writing before signing. Julian asked why Bernard stopped paying and where the trail of the lump sum would be kept. Jezebel said the lump came from Islaport Central in gold and draft; the drafts can be traced, the gold is gone and the ledger shows only the withdrawal, and nothing in the household accounts matches it, with no money for the west wing since. She said Bernard kept a second, smaller private strongbox at the same bank in his own name, still sealed, which the bank would not open for a grandson's curiosity without a solicitor, a will clause and probably a sworn statement, and asked whether he remembered a clause she might have missed.
